entry.title: Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users
entry.summary: Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users Website: Our Social What Makes Our Social Different? Millions of people still rely on basic feature phones and low-speed internet connections, for whom mainstream platforms like Facebook or Instagram are practically unusable. Our Social was built to bridge that gap. The platform runs entirely without JavaScript, meaning it loads smoothly on any basic browser — even on the oldest of devices. Pages are lightweight and fast, even on slow 2G or 3G connections. Features You'll Love Our Social offers everything you'd expect from a social network — posting text and images, adding friends, sending messages, liking and commenting on posts, real-time chat, and notifications. The interface is inspired by the classic button-version of Facebook, keeping things simple, familiar, and easy to navigate on small screens. Browse Without an Account One of Our Social's standout features is that anyone can browse public profiles and posts without needing to log in. Creating a free account is only required when you want to post, like, comment, or connect with others. Who Can Join? Anyone can sign up for free. Whether you're on a feature phone, an old Android device, or any browser-equipped gadget, Our Social works seamlessly for you.

entry.title: AI May Write Code, But Developers Still Define the Problem
entry.summary:
AI tools are becoming increasingly capable of generating code. They can already produce functions, classes, and sometimes even entire applications. But they still rely on humans to define some crucial things: the real problem the constraints the trade-offs the system behavior AI can generate code quickly, but it still needs developers to understand the context and purpose of the system. As coding becomes easier with AI assistance, problem definition and system thinking may become even more important skills. The future developer may not necessarily be the fastest coder. It may be the person who understands the *problem space deeply and can reason about solutions clearly.
